Worker observability refers to the ability to monitor and track the performance and behavior of workers in various settings. It involves gathering data on tasks, productivity, and interactions to gain insights into how work is being carried out and how workers are performing.

For example, in a remote work environment, observability tools can track the time spent on tasks, measure productivity, monitor communication patterns, and even provide feedback on work quality. This kind of observability can help managers understand how work is progressing, identify bottlenecks, and support their teams effectively.
